verification_report.summary:
The full supplied proof passes sequential verification relative to the expressly accepted inputs. All hypotheses and internal references were checked, and no critical errors or gaps were found. The convention ddc=i/(2pi) partial bar-partial is consistent throughout. No BMP, PVP, uniform mass bound, finite total extended mass, analytic singularities, or external unbounded domination theorem is used.

For arbitrary smooth real big theta, the auxiliary obstacle u-rho is finite almost everywhere and bounded below after rho<=0. The accepted bounded-below-envelope lemma therefore gives bounded p=P_{a omega}(u-rho). Contact support is invoked only in the Hermitian background a omega. Canonical representatives give p+rho<=u, and its theta-current is the sum of a omega+ddc p and the positive current theta+ddc rho-a omega. The mixed-product comparison is valid on common finite local levels even when theta is not semipositive: locally one can truncate rho against h-k with theta-a omega+ddc h>=0, rather than assume constant truncations preserve that background. Locality, positivity and arbitrary-background ordered contact give the displayed inequalities; increasing exhaustion and absence of pluripolar mass complete them. The positive mass of the bounded Hermitian potential p then proves positive mass for u. No uniform lower bound is asserted.

Bounded domination uses bounded envelopes w_b and finite measures for each fixed b. The coefficients b^{-n} and (1-b^{-1})^n are correct. Choosing the latter greater than c makes the contact mass vanish on {u<v}; individual non-collapsing supplies sup w_b>=-C. The displayed lower bound for the normalized L1 norm on the fixed positive-volume strict set is correct and contradicts normalized compactness.

Every positive multiple of theta is big, with witness given by the same multiple of rho. In the singular-zero lemma, v<=u+C and v_delta<=v give the constant lower competitor for p=P_{(1-delta)theta}(u-v_delta). Its boundedness and contact support are justified. Positive mixed products and ordered contact transfer the zero-measure hypothesis to {p<0}. The already proved bounded domination applies to p and zero in the non-collapsing background (1-delta)theta, yielding u>=v_delta.

For singular strict domination, the maximum reduction preserves the strict-set inequality and gives u<=v<=u+C. The competitor u-(b-1)C makes each p_b genuine and equivalent in ordinary singularities to u. For fixed b, all measures restricted to {u,v,p_b>-k} are finite restrictions of fixed bounded truncation measures. Thus the cancellation with (1-b^{-1})^n>c is legitimate on each level; continuity from below extends the vanishing without subtracting infinities. Remaining contact mass lies on {p_b=u}. Applying the zero lemma to (p_b,u) gives the fixed lower barrier P_{delta theta}(u). A finite strict point supplies a positive-volume set E, and integer b permits a single pluripolar exceptional set. The inequalities P_{delta theta}(u)<=p_b<=v-ba on E contradict the barrier's L1 integrability.

Exponential order follows by multiplying the weighted inequality by the finite positive weight e^{lambda u} off the poles, restricting to {u<v-t}, and applying strict domination to (u,v-t) with c=e^{-lambda t}. These operations are valid for extended measures. Genuineness of a smaller-background envelope passes under bounded changes by translating a competitor, which justifies applying the result in both directions for uniqueness in the stated ordinary singularity type.

The reference searches were followed by primary-source verification. The bounded statement and exponential consequence match [GL22, Proposition 2.8 and Corollary 2.9](https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf). The singular statements match [ALS26, Theorem 3.11, Lemma 3.12 and Corollary 3.13(i)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1), whose measure framework explicitly allows infinite total mass. [GL23-equations, Definition 1.6 and Theorem 1.11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.01938) require analytic singularities and do not directly cover the first proposition's generality; the supplied auxiliary-envelope proof independently establishes that extension.
